goal.text: Personal data of hospital staff and named patients protected

query.organization_type: medium-sized distributor with an order portal and an LLM-based ordering assistant

kpis.text: Personal data fields classified with a documented purpose (100%)
Patient identifiers stored outside named-patient order records (0)
Data subject requests closed (within the legal deadline)

beliefs: Named-patient orders contain a patient name and medical record number
constraints: Patient identifiers are not sent to the language model provider

ranked_patterns.relevance: Most relevant: its IT goal 'Personal data minimized and classified' maps almost directly onto G06-K1 (fields classified with a documented purpose) and G06-K2 (no patient identifiers outside named-patient order records). Its data inventory, purpose/retention discipline and masking of personal data in non-production systems transfer to the distributor's order portal, and its conflict resolution (keep aggregated history, delete identifiers) is the template for limiting patient identifiers.

Second: 'Data subject requests fulfilled' is the direct source for G06-K3 (requests closed within the legal deadline). Its request register, identity verification before release, and the Data Protection Officer / Customer Service Agent split adapt to hospital staff and named patients, with the Sales Administrator taking the front-office role.

Third: it governs an LLM-based assistant and already carries the constraint that customer personal data is not sent to the model provider beyond the session, which is the pattern for the query constraint 'Patient identifiers are not sent to the language model provider'. Its change register and AI risk review adapt to the LLM-based ordering assistant and the AI Product Owner actor.

Fourth and weakest on subject matter (expiry control, not privacy), but relevant for domain fit: it is a hospital pharmacy pattern whose structure of capturing controlled attributes at receipt and reserving release decisions for a pharmacist adapts to capturing patient identifiers only at order intake and restricting access to named-patient records to the Responsible Pharmacist.

elements.text: Maintain a data inventory that records, for every personal data field of hospital staff and named patients in the order portal and the ordering assistant, its purpose, legal basis and retention period
elements.justification: Adapts 'Maintain a data inventory with purpose and retention per field'; it is the operation that produces the 100% classification figure measured by G06-K1.

elements.text: Review and re-approve the classification of each personal data field whenever a portal or assistant release changes the data collected
elements.justification: Keeps the 100% target of G06-K1 stable over time, following the pattern's rule that no field may exist without a documented purpose.

elements.text: Mask or pseudonymize patient names and medical record numbers in all test, training and non-production copies of the order data
elements.justification: Direct adaptation of 'Mask personal data in non-production systems'; non-production copies are a main source of identifiers stored outside named-patient order records.

elements.text: Scan order records, exports, attachments, logs and assistant conversation stores for patient identifiers held outside named-patient order records and delete or relocate every finding
elements.justification: Adapts the pattern's minimization and identifier-deletion conflict resolution to the query's zero target for identifiers stored outside named-patient order records.

elements.text: Register and verify the identity of each data subject request received from hospital staff or from a named patient before any data is released
elements.justification: Adapts 'Register and verify each data subject request'; registration and verification are the first steps that make a request closable within the legal deadline.

elements.text: Export, correct or erase the requester's personal data and close the request with evidence before the legal deadline
elements.justification: Adapts 'Export or erase the customer's data'; it is the completion step counted by G06-K3.

elements.text: Redact patient names and medical record numbers from prompts and retrieval context before the ordering assistant sends any request to the language model provider
elements.justification: Operationalizes the query constraint using the pattern's rule that customer personal data is not sent to the model provider.

elements.text: Keep a model and prompt change register and approve, before release, every assistant change that affects which personal data is processed
elements.justification: Adapts 'Keep a model and prompt change register' so that privacy impact of assistant changes stays attributable and reviewable.

elements.text: Capture patient name and medical record number only at intake of a named-patient order and store them solely in that order record
elements.justification: Adapts 'Record batch and expiry at receipt' (capture a controlled attribute once, at a single defined point) to patient identifiers, which is what keeps G06-K2 at zero.

elements.text: Data Protection Officer
elements.justification: Pattern actor reused unchanged; owns the data inventory, the classification decisions and the overall privacy goal.

elements.text: Sales Administrator (front-office handler of data subject requests)
elements.justification: Takes the role of the pattern's Customer Service Agent, adapted to the distributor's actor list in scope.

elements.text: IT Security Officer (system owner role for the order portal data stores)
elements.justification: Adapts the pattern's System Owner; executes masking and the removal of identifiers from stores outside named-patient order records.

elements.text: AI Product Owner
elements.justification: Pattern actor reused; accountable for the prompt redaction filter and the model and prompt change register of the ordering assistant.

elements.text: Responsible Pharmacist
elements.justification: Adapts the 'Pharmacist in Charge' authority role; authorizes access to named-patient order records containing identifiers.

elements.text: Quality Assurance Officer
elements.justification: Query actor in scope; verifies in the regulated quality system that the classification evidence behind G06-K1 is complete and auditable.

elements.text: Data inventory of personal data fields with purpose, legal basis and retention
elements.justification: Pattern resource 'Data inventory' reused; it is the record from which the 100% classification KPI is read.

elements.text: Masking and pseudonymization tool for non-production copies of order data
elements.justification: Pattern resource 'Masking tool' reused to support the zero target for identifiers held outside named-patient order records.

elements.text: Data subject request register with verification evidence and deadline tracking
elements.justification: Pattern resource 'Request register' reused, extended with deadline tracking because G06-K3 is measured against the legal deadline.

elements.text: Prompt redaction filter of the ordering assistant
elements.justification: Adapted from the pattern's governance of model interactions; it is the technical means that enforces the query constraint on patient identifiers.

elements.text: Model and prompt change register of the ordering assistant
elements.justification: Pattern resource 'Change register' reused so that every assistant change affecting personal data is approved and traceable.

elements.text: Named-patient orders contain a patient name and a medical record number
elements.justification: Stated in the query; it is the assumption that justifies treating named-patient order records as the only permitted location for identifiers.

elements.text: Hospital staff and patients expect their personal data to be used only for handling and delivering their orders
elements.justification: Adapts the pattern belief 'Customers expect data to be used only for their orders'; it motivates requiring a documented purpose for every field.

elements.text: Regulation requires traceable records for every named-patient supply, so identifiers cannot simply be deleted from the order record
elements.justification: Adapts 'Regulation requires batch records for every medicine'; it explains why G06-K2 targets identifiers outside the order record rather than inside it.

elements.text: Patient identifiers are never sent to the language model provider, in prompts, retrieval context or logs
elements.justification: Query constraint, grounded in the pattern constraint that customer personal data is not sent to the model provider beyond the session.

elements.text: Identity of the requester is verified before any personal data is released or erased
elements.justification: Pattern constraint reused unchanged; it prevents a fast closure of a request from becoming a data breach.

elements.text: Personal data of hospital staff and named patients is retained no longer than its documented purpose and the regulated traceability period require
elements.justification: Pattern constraint reused and widened to the regulated context; it binds each classified field to a bounded retention.

elements.text: Only the Responsible Pharmacist and explicitly authorized Sales Administrators may access named-patient order records containing identifiers
elements.justification: Adapts 'Only a pharmacist may release quarantined medicines' into an access restriction that keeps identifiers from spreading outside the order record.

output.rational_statement: G06 serves the parent goal G01 'Regulated order-to-delivery controlled and secure' by making the personal data that flows through the order portal and the LLM-based ordering assistant explicit, bounded and answerable: classifying every field with a documented purpose (G06-K1) is the precondition for all other privacy controls, because a field that is not inventoried can neither be masked, retained correctly, nor located when a data subject asks; that inventory in turn enables the masking, intake-only capture and scanning tasks that drive patient identifiers stored outside named-patient order records to zero (G06-K2), which is what allows the order-to-delivery chain to remain traceable for regulated named-patient supplies without spreading identifiers into test systems, exports or assistant conversation stores; and the request register with identity verification lets the Data Protection Officer and Sales Administrator close data subject requests within the legal deadline (G06-K3) precisely because the inventory tells them where the data is. The prompt redaction filter and the model and prompt change register extend the same control to the ordering assistant, enforcing the constraint that patient identifiers never reach the language model provider, so that the security half of G01 is not undermined by the automation that supports its speed.
